title: The missing pieces of workflow automation — Shirsha Chaudhuri, Thomson Reuters Labs
talk_summary: A Thomson Reuters Labs practitioner argues that automating individual tasks is insufficient and that reimagining end-to-end workflows with agents is blocked by missing pieces: connectors to legacy systems, reliability/ROI proof, domain visionaries, standardization, distributed context, collaborative UX, governance, human control, and agent lifecycle. It is a high-level enterprise framing talk with no concrete implementation details, metrics, or reproducible mechanisms.

takeaways.technique: Standardized agent packaging and deployment contract
takeaways.what_they_do: Calls for a common standard for how agents are built, packaged, and deployed so they can be composed into workflows rather than bespoke one-offs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need a certain level of standardization right we need to be able to say this is how agents will be built this is how they are packaged this is how they're deployed

takeaways.what_they_do: Design workflows so some steps are deterministic and others are agent-autonomous, giving humans control at the right moments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to have certain steps which are deterministic and certain steps which the agent can control on its own

takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that agent context is scattered across tickets, logs, chat, and business systems, and correlating a single transaction across them is a core blocker.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you correlate a single transaction across Ross These systems becomes often a stumbling part

takeaways.technique: Reliability as a zero-or-one gate before replacing manual hours
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames adoption as binary: stakeholders ask whether the agent can fully replace paid manual hours, making reliability the gating metric.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's a zero or one call right am I going to continue to need to have to pay manual hours

takeaways.technique: Governance mapped onto agent architecture layers
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues existing ethics/responsibility governance must be translated into specific levels of the agent architecture rather than staying policy-only.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you translate that into different levels of your agent architecture
